what_its_for: Esomeprazole reduces the amount of acid your stomach makes. It is used to treat heartburn, acid reflux (GERD), stomach ulcers, and conditions where the stomach makes too much acid. It can also help protect your stomach lining when you take certain pain medicines like ibuprofen or naproxen.
how_to_take: Swallow the capsule whole with a full glass of water. Take it at least 30 to 60 minutes BEFORE eating, usually in the morning. If you have trouble swallowing the capsule, you can open it and sprinkle the small beads inside onto a spoonful of soft applesauce. Swallow right away without chewing the beads. Do NOT crush or chew the capsule or the beads inside. If taking the powder packet, mix it with water as directed on the label.
dosing: The usual adult dose for heartburn and acid reflux (GERD) is 20 mg to 40 mg once a day. For stomach ulcers or more serious conditions, your doctor may prescribe a higher dose or twice-daily dosing. For over-the-counter use (Nexium 24HR), the usual dose is 20 mg once daily for 14 days. Always follow your doctor's or pharmacist's instructions exactly, as your dose depends on your specific condition.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but only if it is still before your next meal. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Do NOT take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Store in the original container with the lid tightly closed. Keep out of reach of children. Do not store in the bathroom.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking esomeprazole at the same time as certain other medicines, especially Plavix (clopidogrel), methotrexate, or HIV medicines, as esomeprazole can affect how these drugs work. Avoid drinking excessive amounts of alcohol, as it can worsen stomach irritation. Avoid foods and drinks that trigger your heartburn, such as spicy foods, citrus, tomatoes, chocolate, caffeine, and fatty or fried foods. Do not take more than prescribed or for longer than recommended without talking to your doctor.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience: severe diarrhea that is watery or bloody, muscle cramps, spasms, or weakness (this could be a sign of low magnesium), bone pain or frequent fractures (especially with long-term use), symptoms of a serious allergic reaction such as rash, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing, new or worsening heartburn after 14 days of over-the-counter use, unintended weight loss, trouble swallowing, vomiting blood, or black/tarry stools. Also let your doctor know if your symptoms do not improve after 4 weeks of treatment.
when_it_works: You may start to feel some relief from heartburn within 1 to 4 days of starting esomeprazole. However, it may take 1 to 4 weeks of regular use to get the full benefit, especially for healing ulcers or treating GERD. Take it every day as directed, even if you start feeling better, unless your doctor tells you to stop sooner.
special_populations: Older adults (65+): Esomeprazole is generally safe for older adults, but long-term use may increase the risk of bone fractures, low magnesium levels, and certain infections. Talk to your doctor about how long you should take it. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Talk to your doctor before using esomeprazole if you are pregnant or breastfeeding, as it should only be used if clearly needed. Children: Esomeprazole can be used in children as young as 1 month old for certain conditions, but only under a doctor's guidance. Kidney or liver problems: Patients with severe liver disease may need a lower dose. Let your doctor know about any kidney or liver issues before starting this medicine.
